notes: 2026 rate schedules (revised May 20, 2026) from Maine Revenue Services; top bracket includes the new 2% income tax surcharge (36 M.R.S. 5111(7)) on Maine taxable income over $1,000,000 single, $750,000 married filing separately, $1,500,000 joint/HoH, folded in as 7.15% + 2% = 9.15%.
Standard deduction phases out for Maine AGI over $102,250 single/MFS, $153,400 HoH, $204,550 joint, fully gone over a $75,000/$112,500/$150,000 range. Modeled.
Personal exemption ($5,300 each for taxpayer and spouse) phases out for Maine AGI over $341,000 single, $375,050 HoH, $409,150 joint over a $125,000 range. Modeled.

Not modeled: Maine income modifications (pension deduction, decoupling add-backs for bonus/qualified production property depreciation and R&E expensing), dependent exemption credit, property tax fairness credit, sales tax fairness credit, Maine EITC, and the 2026 affordability-payment subtraction.
Maine conforms to the IRC as amended through Dec 31, 2025 (P.L. 2025, c. 650, Pt. K).

seDeduction.note: Maine starts from federal AGI, so the deductible half of SE tax (an above-the-line federal adjustment) is already excluded.

seHealthInsurance.note: The self-employed health insurance deduction is an above-the-line federal adjustment inherited through federal AGI.

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) deductions are above-the-line federal adjustments inherited through federal AGI.

qbi.note: The federal QBI deduction is taken after AGI, so it does not reduce the state base.

localIncomeTax.note: Maine municipalities do not levy a local income tax.

estimatedTax.threshold: Estimated Maine income tax, after withholding and allowable credits, of $1,000 or more (and prior-year liability also $1,000 or more)
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Pay at least the smaller of 100% of the prior year's tax (if the prior year was 12 months) or 90% of the current year's tax. Special rule: 'unusual event income' ($500,000+ increase over the same period of the prior year) requires 90% of the tax on that income and cannot use the prior-year rule.

businessCosts.annualReportFee: $85 domestic LLC annual report, due June 1 every year (31 M.R.S. 1680)
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: None for LLCs and sole proprietors (Maine's franchise tax applies to financial institutions)
